alignments.note: Genitive-absolute subject of the participle, rendered by the English subject pronoun.
Intensifying kai realized by *also*, its own unit under rule 65.
Compound participle rendered by verb plus the particle answering to the syn- prefix; rule 17 heads on the lexical verb *helping*, which carries the sense, not on *together*.

Discontinuous *on ... behalf* wrap around the possessive, one unit under rule 15. Rule 78's settled *for ... sake* precedent heads such a wrap on the prepositional word rather than on the frame's supplied noun. A head on *behalf* remains defensible if rule 67's divided case for a contiguous frame is read as reaching this shape.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive standing inside the hyper frame.

Rule 76: hymon is already spent on *ye* as subject of the genitive absolute, so it is not available to take the supplied possessive and the article carries *your*, with the case preposition *by* riding along under rules 20 and 21, headed on the determiner. Giving *your* to hymon and emptying the article under rule 20 proper is the competing reading.
Noun stands alone, its determiner and case preposition being on the article.
Purpose conjunction realized by the English complementizer introducing its clause (rule 40).

Article in attributive position governing charisma across the interposed prepositional phrase (rule 57), and standing in front of its noun, so it takes the English *the* and leaves the noun bare (rule 31's preceding-article clause).

Rule 62: the verbless prepositional phrase's supplied lexical verb *bestowed* rides with the preposition, and rule 17 heads the unit on the word realizing the preposition, not on the supplied verb. Attaching *bestowed* to charisma is the competing reading, but the ASV spends *gift* on that lexeme and *bestowed* is supplied only to attach the phrase.
Accusative pronoun governed by eis.
Head noun stands bare, its determiner being on the article that precedes it.

Complex frame *by means of* on an expressed proper preposition; rule 95 confirms dia is proper, so rule 67 leaves the head divided and the 2 Corinthians neighbours (2CO.7.4, 2CO.7.14) head the prepositional word. A head on *means* remains defensible.
Substantival adjective governed by dia; the ASV writes a bare *many* with no supplied noun.

Rule 91: eucharisteo heads on *thanks*, the word the corpus spends on the lexeme, with *may be given* as rule 9 helpers. The supplied *for* comes from the English passive recast — the Greek makes to charisma the nominative subject — so no Greek case or preposition answers to it and it stays with the verb whose argument structure licenses it, discontinuously under rule 15. Giving *for the* to the article under rule 21 is the competing reading.
Preposition realized by *by*, its phrase moved to the end of the English clause.
Attributive adjective modifying prosopon.
Anarthrous noun with no supplied determiner.
Second *on ... behalf* wrap, analysed exactly as the first under rule 24.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive standing inside the hyper frame.

review_notes: Reviewed unchanged. The partition is complete and disjoint: all 20 source IDs and all 31 target IDs occur exactly once, every unit is aligned with nonempty arrays, and every head is a member of its own array.
